blocks.text:
You’ll board the motor vessel in Manaus. After meeting the crew and getting to know the boat, you’ll set off upriver on the Amazon.

Along the way, your guide will explain the Amazon ecosystem, the rivers’ seasonal floods, and the region’s forests and wildlife. On your first day, you’ll leave the city waterfront behind and reach quieter stretches of the river.

After dinner, you’ll head out along the riverbank. Your guide will use torches to look for caimans and other nocturnal wildlife. You may spot nightjars, sloths, snakes, frogs and other animals that are active after sunset.

Overnight aboard the vessel.
An orange sunset reflects on calm water between the silhouettes of trees
Dark branches by the bank and a bright strip of evening sky above the water
Lake Janauacá, rainforest, a local community and piranha fishing

Early in the morning, you’ll canoe on Lake Janauacá. This is a good time to watch for birds and river wildlife. Amazon pink river dolphins are found here.

After breakfast, you’ll take a walk in the forest. Your guide will introduce you to plants of the humid tropics and explain how local people use the natural resources of the Amazon.

Later, you’ll meet residents of the lake area. They grow cassava and fruit trees, fish, and collect Brazil nuts, rubber and other forest products.

In the afternoon, you’ll fish for piranhas. You may also see hoatzins and large flocks of herons during the outing.

After dinner, you’ll go out by canoe again. At night, you can hear insects and frogs in the forest. On a clear evening, the stars of the Southern Hemisphere are clearly visible above the river.

Overnight aboard the vessel.
